title: Shepherd, trader, and a pact for justice
hook: Before anyone called him a prophet, they called him "the trustworthy".

screens.text: **Before anyone called him a prophet, they called him "the trustworthy."** How does a poor orphan earn a name like that in a whole city? One job, one deal, one promise at a time.
**A shepherd for small wages.** He herded sheep for the people of Makkah, for a few coins. He said that every prophet Allah sent had herded sheep [Bukhari 2262].
bubbles: Think about the job: long days, other people's animals, little pay, and nobody watching.

screens.prompt: What can years of shepherding train in a person? Pick all that apply.

options.feedback: Yes. Sheep wander and dawdle. You can't rush them, and you can't leave them.
Yes. A shepherd watches the slow and the hurt ones, not just the strong.
Yes. Out in the hills, only you and Allah know if you did the job well.
Not quite. Shepherding was humble, low-paid work. That was part of its lesson.

screens.text: **A trader people trusted.** As a young man he also worked in trade [IslamQA 11575; Dar al-Ifta 169]. He dealt honestly, and people noticed. His people gave him a name: al-Amin, "the trustworthy" [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 23].
bubbles: He never worshipped the idols around the Ka'bah, and he stayed away from alcohol and the immoral behaviour common around him [IslamQA 11575; Dar al-Ifta 167].

events.title: Shepherd
events.text: Herds sheep for the people of Makkah for a few coins [Bukhari 2262].

events.title: A pact for the wronged
events.text: Witnesses Makkan clans swear to stand with anyone wronged in Makkah [Qalam ep. 19; Dar al-Ifta 174].

events.title: Trader
events.text: Works in trade, at first locally, the early biographers say [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 20].

events.title: Al-Amin
events.text: His people call him "the trustworthy" [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 23].

events.title: A job offer
events.text: A respected businesswoman named Khadijah hears about his honesty [IslamQA 11575].

screens.text: **A pact for the wronged.** When he was about twenty, the early biographers say, a cheated visiting trader called out for help at the Ka'bah. Several clans met and swore to stand with anyone wronged in Makkah [Qalam ep. 19; Dar al-Ifta 174].
bubbles: It was called *Hilf al-Fudul*, often translated "the Pact of the Virtuous". He was there to witness it.
The trader got his goods back, the early biographers say. Being an outsider no longer meant being unprotected [Qalam ep. 19].

screens.prompt: What did the clans who swore Hilf al-Fudul promise?

options.text: To stand with anyone wronged in Makkah
options.feedback: Right. Even a visitor with no clan of his own in Makkah would be backed against the powerful.

options.text: To protect only their own clan members
options.feedback: Not quite. That was the old way. The pact covered anyone wronged in Makkah, outsiders included.

options.text: To go to war with the cheater's tribe
options.feedback: Not quite. It was a pledge to get justice for the wronged, not a war.

screens.text: **Character before a title.** He was al-Amin for years before anyone called him a prophet. You don't need to know much **fiqh** (the detailed rules of practice) to be the most trustworthy person at your job or school. That part starts today.

screens.situation: Chris works in a phone store. His manager tells him to say a returned phone "was working fine when it left the store", though they both know it wasn't. Chris has been Muslim three weeks.

options.text: Politely say he won't tell the customer something untrue, and offer to help sort out the return
options.feedback: Yes. Calm, respectful, and honest. That's how al-Amin got his name: one deal at a time.

options.text: Go along with it; he's new and doesn't know the rulings yet
options.feedback: Not quite. Honesty doesn't need advanced study. The Prophet ﷺ was trusted long before any rulings came.

options.text: Quit on the spot and tell the manager off
options.feedback: Not quite. No drama needed. A calm, honest no keeps his integrity and his job, if he can.

screens.prompt: Builds trust, or spends it? Sort these everyday moments.

items.text: Giving back extra change a cashier handed you by mistake
items.why: Small, unseen honesty is exactly how al-Amin's name was earned.

items.text: Calling in sick to go to a party
items.why: A small lie, but people remember. Trust is lost faster than it's built.
Keeping what you're trusted with is part of being trustworthy.

items.text: Rounding up hours on a timesheet
items.why: It's taking pay you didn't earn, even if nobody checks.

chips: Why did every prophet herd sheep?
Didn't a monk recognise him as a boy?
My boss wants me to bend the truth. What do I do?

steps: Keep one small promise exactly as you said it
Return or pay back anything you owe: money, an item, a reply

screens.text: Long before the title of prophet, he earned the name "the trustworthy". Your character can start speaking for your faith today.
Next episode: Khadijah, a businesswoman who hires him, and then proposes.

check.prompt: What did the people of Makkah call him before he was a prophet?

options.feedback: Right. He earned it through years of honest work as a shepherd and trader.
Not quite. He was a humble shepherd and trader. They called him al-Amin, the trustworthy.

options.text: A pact of Makkan clans to stand with anyone wronged in Makkah
options.feedback: Right. He witnessed it at about twenty, after a visiting trader was cheated.

options.text: A trade deal between Makkah and Syria
options.feedback: Not quite. It was a pledge to stand with anyone wronged in Makkah, prompted by a cheated trader.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- He herded sheep for the people of Makkah for a few qirats (small coins), and said every prophet herded sheep [Bukhari 2262].
- As a young man he worked in trade [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 20; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 3]. Qalam ep. 20 notes he traded locally on commission before working for Khadijah.
- At about twenty he witnessed *Hilf al-Fudul*: a visiting trader (of the tribe of Zubayd) was cheated by a Makkan who refused to pay; he called out at the Ka'bah; clans met and swore to stand with anyone wronged in Makkah, whatever their tribe; the goods were returned [Qalam ep. 19; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 8]. Tell the detail as "the early biographers say". (Dar al-Ifta part 2 describes it as a peace treaty after the Fijar war, a different framing.)
- His people called him al-Amin, "the trustworthy" [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 23].
- He never worshipped idols and avoided alcohol and immoral behaviour [IslamQA 11575; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 1].

**Likely questions**
- *"Didn't a Christian monk (Bahira) recognise him as a future prophet?"* It's "a well-known story whose chain scholars consider weak", and the reports differ on the details, so this track leaves it out. (scholar question Q43)
- *"Did he say he'd join the pact again in Islam?"* There is a report of this outside the six hadith collections this program uses, so don't quote it. Say the pact is remembered as an example of standing up for justice.
- *"Why did prophets herd sheep?"* The hadith states the fact [Bukhari 2262]; scholars reflect that it trains patience, care and humility. Present that as reflection, not as his words.
- *"My boss wants me to bend the truth."* Honesty is core [see Day 63]; suggest a calm, respectful no and an honest alternative. Job-specific dilemmas (whether to stay in a job) go to the imam.
- *"Did he worship idols before Islam?"* No; the sources say he never did.

**Escalate:** whether to leave a job over dishonest practices or haram work (Q31 territory).

**Don't**
- Don't tell the Bahira story as fact.
- Don't quote the "I would answer it in Islam" saying as a hadith.
- Don't use him to shame the convert's past ("he never did X, so you should feel bad").
sourcesMd:

- [IslamQA 11575, *Who Is Muhammad?*](https://islamqa.info/en/answers/11575): trade, al-Amin, never worshipping idols, avoiding alcohol and immorality.
- Dar al-Ifta Egypt: [*A Closer Look at the World before the Advent of Prophet Muhammad (part 1)*](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/article/details/167/a-closer-look-at-the-world-before-the-advent-of-prophet-muhammadpart-1); [*The Divine Preparation of Prophet Muhammad (part 3)*](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/article/details/169/the-divine-preparation-of-prophet-muhammad-part-3) (trade); [*The Art of Negotiations (part 8)*](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/article/details/174/the-art-of-negotiations-a-prophetic-examplepart-8) (the Fudul alliance supports the unjustly treated).
